items.text: Facebook Watch opened a PAW-trait gallery in London and launched it World’s Greatest Dog competition. There are pictures of famous, rare, influencer , and hero dogs for humans and dogs to look at, as the pictures are hung at both human and dog heights, so both you and your pup can enjoy the exhibition. To enter the competition and maybe win $100,000, you just upload a video of your dog to Facebook Watch. Even if you do not win, your dog can become an Internet celebrity, and what’s more , Facebook will give $1 to a dog charity for every uploaded video. In the UK, it is the Battersea Cats and Dogs Home. Difficult words: PAW-trait (this is a pun, a type of joke: paw-trait sounds like portrait, and paw is a dog’s foot), influencer (a lot of people watch an influencer, so what they do/say influences people – can change what/how they think), what’s more (additionally). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Facebook Watch opened a gallery for dogs in London. There are pictures of famous, rare, influencer , and hero dogs. People hung the pictures at both human and dog heights, so both you and your pup can enjoy the exhibition. Aside from visiting the gallery, you can also upload a video of your dog to Facebook Watch. Facebook will give $1 to a dog charity for every uploaded video, and you can win $100,000. In the UK, the charity which is getting help is the Battersea Cats and Dogs Home. Difficult words: influencer (a lot of people watch an influencer, so what they do/say influences people – can change what/how they think). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Facebook Watch opens a gallery in London. It is a gallery of pictures of dogs. There are pictures of famous, rare , influencer , and hero dogs. You can come with your dog. The pictures are at human and dog heights . You can also upload a video to Facebook Watch. For every video, Facebook gives $1 to a dog charity. If you upload a video, you can win $100,000, too. Difficult words: rare (of a special type), influencer (a lot of people watch an influencer, so what they do/say influences people – can change what/how they think), height (how high the picture is hung). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Argentinian striker Emiliano Sala was flying from Nantes (France) to Cardiff (Wales) when his plane disappeared from radar on 21st of January. Peopled called off the official search operation on 24th, but with the help of crowd-funding donations (which collected over €370,000) Sala’s family hired a professional shipwreck hunter to continue the search for the missing plane. The private search was underway since February 3rd and on February 7th, people found Sala’s body, identified it and brought it to land. Tributes came in from around the world. The footballer played for the Football Club Nantes from 2015 to 2019 when he moved to the Cardiff City Football Club. Sadly, he died even before his first training with the new team. The Cardiff City and FC Nantes managers gave emotional press conferences last Friday, saying that it was a loss, not only to everyone in football, but to the whole sporting community. FC Nantes is going to have a memorial service and will retire the No. 9 jersey in his honour. The body of the pilot of the light plane has not yet been found. Difficult words: striker (a forward or attacker in football), tribute (a message that you are feel emotions about someone or something and to show that you liked the thing or the person), jersey (the shirt worn by a player). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Argentinian footballer Emiliano Sala was flying from Nantes, France, to Cardiff, Wales, when his plane went off radar . This was back on 21st of January. There was an official search operation, but people cancelled it on 24th of January. Sala’s family wanted to find him, and they got help from people who gave them over €370,000. They used the money to hire a professional shipwreck hunter to find the missing plane. The private search found the body of Sala on February 7th. Tributes came in from around the world. The footballer played for the Football Club Nantes from 2015 to 2019 when he moved to the Cardiff City Football Club. Sadly, he died even before his first training with the new team. Difficult words: off radar (disappear from the radar), hire (employ, give money to do some work), tribute (a message that you are sad that somebody died, a message to show that you like someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Emiliano Sala is a football player. He is Argentinian. He plays for a French football club from 2015 to 2019. In 2019, he wants to start playing for a British football club. He is on a plane from France to Britain. It is a small, light plane. It crashes into the sea. This happens on 21st of January. He never starts playing for the new team. It takes a long time to find his plane. On February 7th, people find Sala’s body. Tributes come in from around the world. Difficult words: tribute (a message to show that you like someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Football players in their early teens were sleeping in the facilities of a football club in Rio de Janeiro when a fire broke out. Ten people died and three were injured after the fire spread through the training grounds . People are investigating the incident – it is possible that a short circuit caused the fire. Difficult words: facility (a building or buildings for a specific use), grounds (an area for a specific use), short circuit (when an electrical thing fails and the electricity starts a fire). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Teenage football players were sleeping in the facilities of a football club when a fire broke out . This happened in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The fire grew, killed ten people and injured three. People are investigating why the fire started, and it is possible that there was a short circuit . Difficult words: facility (a building or buildings for a specific use), broke out (start), short circuit (when an electric machine fails and the electricity starts a fire). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Young football players are at a training camp. A fire starts at night. This happens when they are sleeping. Ten people die. Three are injured. This happens in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. People want to know why the fire starts . Maybe there is a short circuit . Difficult words: start (begin), short circuit (when an electrical thing fails and the electricity starts a fire). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Heavy rain caused a mudslide in a spot known as El Choro in Bolivia. The potentially deadly mudslide wreaked havoc , forcing people to run to safety. It wiped out trees and buried cars, but there were no reported casualties . Difficult words: spot (a place), wreak havoc (do a lot of damage), casualty (a person killed in an accident). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Heavy rain caused a mudslide in Bolivia. Someone filmed it at a place known as El Choro. The mudslide wiped out trees and buried cars, but nobody died. People ran away from it. Difficult words: mudslide (when a mix of water and earth moves and destroys things), wipe out (destroy, break), bury (cover in mud, put underground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

It rains heavily in Bolivia. This causes a mudslide . People film it. It destroys trees and cars. People run away from it. Nobody dies. Difficult words: cause (make), mudslide (when a mix of water and earth moves and destroys things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At least eight people died and nearly 30 others were injured in a building fire in Paris last week. The blaze broke out in the 16th district, one of the calmest and wealthiest of the city. More than 200 firefighters were on the scene, putting out the fire and evacuating the residents. French prosecutors are still investigating the cause, but a woman who lived in the building was arrested in connection with the blaze. Difficult words: blaze (a fire), prosecutor (police or someone who finds out if you did something illegal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There was a fire in a building in Paris last week. Eight or more people died and nearly 30 people were injured. The fire broke out in the 16th Paris district , which is a calm and wealthy part of the city. More than 200 firefighters were on the scene. They put out the fire and evacuated people. The police still do not know the cause of the fire. However, they arrested one woman who lived in the building. Difficult words: break out (start), district (an area, a part of a city), wealthy (rich people live there). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a fire in Paris. A building is on fire. Eight or more people die. Thirty people are injured. The fire is in the 16th Paris district . Normally, this district is calm. Two hundred firefighters stop this fire. They evacuate people, too. The police do not know the cause of the fire. However, they arrest one woman. Difficult words: district (an area, a part of a city), evacuate (move away from the danger), cause (why and how something starts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US is challenging the lawfulness of Venezuela’s president, Nicolas Maduro, and the US sanctioned Venezuela’s state-run oil company. This is in an effort to shift money over to Juan Gaido, the opposition leader. Maduro is ignoring the world’s requests for him to cede power to Gaido. President Trump asked Elliott Abrams to lead the country’s response to the crisis. In the 1980s, Abrams wanted to overthrow Nicaragua’s government which means that he might want to try to overthrow Maduro. The hope is to get Venezuela’s military to switch sides from Maduro because the military would not fight the US. However, this can be a problem, as people may not support Gaido if they see the US trying to force a change in Venezuela. Difficult words: sanction (penalise), cede (give something up), overthrow (take over by force). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The US is challenging the legitimacy of Venezuela’s president because he will not step down to another leader who the people voted for. The Venezuelan president is ignoring the world’s requests to give up his power. The American president asked a leader to help America with this problem. This leader wanted to overthrow Nicaragua’s government in the 1980s, which means that he might want to overthrow Venezuela’s government. America hopes to get Venezuela’s military to stop supporting the president there. However, this can backfire if people see this as the US trying to force change. They may not want to support the other leader. Difficult words: legitimacy (lawfulness), overthrow (take over), backfire (when a solution becomes a problem). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The USA is unhappy with Venezuela’s president. People vote for another person to be the president. However, the current president is not stepping down . America has a man who is working on this problem. This man works in the 1980s. He wants to overthrow Nicaragua’s government . It is possible that he wants to overthrow Venezuela’s government, too. However, this is a problem. People around the world may not like that America changes something in Venezuela. Difficult words: step down (stop being a leader), overthrow (take over a government), government (the leaders, the bosses of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US federal law bans the recording of animal torture , but there is no federal law to ban the actual torturing. People have introduced legislation to ban it in Congress in the past, but it has never gone to the vote. Now, representative like Ted Deutch and Vern Buchanan are trying again. The PACT Act (Preventing Animal Cruelty and Torture) would criminalise things like crushing, burning and impaling animals. Those who break the law could face fines and up to seven years in prison. The PACT would exclude things like fishing and hunting. Difficult words: torture (make an animal feel great pain), legislation (laws), impale (spear, cut, stab with a knife). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

It is illegal to films animal torture in the USA, but it is not illegal to torture animals. It may be illegal in some states, but the federal law does not make it illegal everywhere. There is a new law which would make torturing animals illegal everywhere in the USA. It is called the PACT Act (Preventing Animal Cruelty and Torture). If the law passes and people break it, they will have to pay money or go to prison for up to seven years. Difficult words: torture (make an animal feel great pain), federal law (a law which exists everywhere in the USA), pass (when leaders say ‘yes’, this law exists right now). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about a law in the USA. There it is illegal to torture animals and film this. Torturing animals ‘only’ is OK. In some states, it is illegal. In other states, it is legal. There is no federal ban on torturing animals. This can change soon. There is a new law. It is called PACT. If leaders say ‘yes’ to PACT, torturing animals become illegal everywhere in the USA. Difficult words: illegal (people must not do illegal things), torture (make an animal feel great pain), federal ban (a law that makes something illegal in the whole USA). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Italy, heavy rains caused an unusually high tide , and flooding affected parts of Venice’s historic centre. Water levels reached an estimated 113 centimetres, so most tourists and residents resorted to using wooden platforms to cross St Mark’s Square. Some just walked through the water in rubber boots. Sixteen percent of the city was affected. Difficult words: tide (high tide is when water moves towards the land, low tide is when it moves away from land), flooding (too much water), resort to (do something because of a situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Heavy rains in Italy caused an unusually high tide , and parts of Venice’s historic centre were flooded . Water went up by around 113 centimetres so most people walked on wooden platforms . Some just walked through the water in rubber boots. Difficult words: tide (high tide is when water moves towards the land, low tide is when it moves away from land), flood (go under water), platform (a side walk which looks like a small bridges). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

It rains a lot in Italy. This makes the tide very high. The centre of Venice is flooded . The water goes up by around 113 centimetres. People walk on wooden platforms . Some people walk through the water. Difficult words: tide (how high or low the water is), flood (go under water), platform (a side walk which looks like a small bridge). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scottish-British tennis star Andy Murray, has undergone hip surgery to end the painful injury which may have brought the Scot’s professional career to an end. Before the surgery, he admitted, after his first-round loss to Roberto Bautista Agut at the Australian Open, that the tournament could be his last. On his Instagram, Murray said that he felt ‘a bit battered ’ after the operation which included inserting a piece of metal into his pelvic socket . Despite the health problems, he hopes to recover in time to make his final appearance at Wimbledon and retire at the age of 31. Difficult words: battered (injured, sad, tired, not good), pelvic (relating to pelvis – the large bone frame where your legs start), socket (a space for the leg to be connected to the pelvis). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Andy Murray is a British tennis star who was injured and had to have surgery . He last played at the Australian Open where he lost to Roberto Bautista Agut. He said there that this tournament could be his last one because of the injury. Murray had the surgery and he posted an Instagram from the hospital. Doctors put a piece of metal into his pelvis . He hopes to get better and play at Wimbledon, and then he wants to retire at age 31. Difficult words: surgery (an operation; when doctors change your body), tournament (a series of sports games), pelvis (a big bone below your belly that is also where your legs start). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Andy Murray is a British tennis star. He plays at the Australian Open. This can be his last tournament . He is injured. He must have surgery . He has the surgery. Doctors put a piece of metal inside his pelvis . He hopes to get better. He wants to play at Wimbledon. He wants to stop playing at age 31. Difficult words: tournament (a series of tennis games), surgery (an operation; when doctors put something into your body or change your body), pelvis (a big bone below your belly and above where your legs start). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Facebook is expanding its fight against political misinformation to help countries prevent foreign interference in their elections. The company wants to prevent another scandal like the one in 2016, when Russian-linked operations used Facebook to interfere in the U.S. presidential election. Facebook will require advertisers to be authorised before buying political ads, give people more information about the ads and start a searchable public library. The new tools will first launch in the EU before the parliamentary elections, then in India, Ukraine and Israel. They will become available globally before July. The company also set up regional operations centres in Dublin and in Singapore which will add extra ‘defence against fake news, hate speech and voter suppression’. Difficult words: prevent (stop something from happening before it happens), interference (the act of interfering, manipulating, changing), launch (start). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Facebook is trying to prevent political misinformation . In 2016, there was a problem that someone from Russia used Facebook to interfere with the American presidential election. Facebook wants to prevent another problem like this. When somebody wants to buy a political ad, he or she will have to register. Also, Facebook will give people more information about the ads and have a library of the ads. First the new tools will exist in the EU, then in India, Ukraine and Israel. The new tools will start working everywhere before July. The company also set up regional operations centres in Dublin and in Singapore. These will be an extra protection against ‘fake news, hate speech’ and will protect free voting. Difficult words: prevent (stop something from happening before it happens), misinformation (false, not true information, fake news), interfere (manipulate, change). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2016, people in the USA choose their president. A lot of people use Facebook. They see political ads there. These ads influence people. People say that someone from Russia buys these ads. This is a problem. Facebook does not want this to happen again. Workers make Facebook safer. Now you must be authorised to have a political ad on Facebook. People can get more information about the ads, too. First the new, safer Facebook starts in the EU. Then it starts in India, Ukraine and Israel. The new Facebook will be in every country before July. Difficult words: ad (a picture, text or video which shows you some information; for example, which leader to choose or which thing to buy), influence (when you influence somebody, you make them do something), authorise (check and give a license). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Upskirting – taking unauthorised pictures up a woman’s skirt – has been an offence in Scotland since 2010. However, England and Wales have no specific ban against upskirting. The law could change in the two countries after the House of Lords passes a new law. It is all thanks to Gina Martin who started a campaign in 2017 to outlaw the practise, as she had been a victim of upskirting at a music festival in the summer of 2017. Difficult words: offence (an illegal act), ban (if there is a ban on something, it is illegal to do it), outlaw (make illegal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Upskirting is taking unauthorised pictures up a woman’s skirt. In Scotland it became illegal in 2010, but it is not illegal in England and in Wales. However, this can soon change if a new law passes in the House of Lords. The law will make upskirting an offence . This is thanks to Gina Martin who was upskirted at a music festival in the summer of 2017. Later, she started a campaign to outlaw the practise. Difficult words: unauthorised (not give permission), offence (an illegal act), outlaw (make illegal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about upskirting. Upskirting is when people take a picture up a skirt. Some people up skirt women. The women do not want this. They do not say, ‘yes, take my picture’. Upskirting is illegal in Scotland. It is not illegal in England and in Wales. This can change. There is a new law . If it passes , upskirting becomes illegal in England and Wales, too. Difficult words: illegal (something illegal is a crime), law (a document which says what people can or cannot do), pass (make a law and say when it starts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

YouTube is rewriting its algorithms so that fewer conspiracy theory videos will be recommended to users. The company says that its goal is to give users a better experience by reducing content that ‘could misinform users in harmful ways’. For example, this concerns videos which promote phoney miracle cures for serious illnesses, videos which claim that the earth is flat, or videos which make false claims about events like 9/11 (the attack on the World Trade Centre). One user on YouTube, Joshua Cox, commented that YouTube’s move was about censorship. The move may be motivated by criticism which YouTube faced last year – a video suggested that David Hogg, a student who survived a school shooting, was an actor. The video was viewed over 200,000 times before YouTube removed it. The change will affect less than 1 per cent of videos, but users around the world watch an average of 1 billion hours of YouTube videos a day. Difficult words: algorithm (the rules which a program or a computer follows), conspiracy theory (a term which is used for explanations of events which are different from explanations that most people believe; or explanations about things which are not possibly true), phoney (fake). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

YouTube tries to recommend to you videos which it thinks that you are interested in. Nobody chooses these videos for you, as software does this. YouTube is now changing the software to recommend fewer conspiracy theory videos. YouTube says that this change will affect less than 1 per cent of videos. However, users around the world watch around 1 billion hours of YouTube videos a day. YouTube says that it is doing this to give people a better experience. What type of conspiracy videos will not be recommended? For example, videos which try to sell you fake medicine, videos which say that the earth is flat, or videos which say lies about events like 9/11 (the attacks on the World Trade Centre on September 11th 2011). Some people may not like this. For example, they may think that the earth is not flat, but they think that videos about 9/11 can be true. They see YouTube’s move as an act of censorship . Difficult words: recommend (suggest, offer), conspiracy theory (an idea that people use to explain events which are different from explanations that most people believe; or explanations about things which are not possibly true), censorship (censoring – limiting what people can watch, write, read, or say). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

YouTube knows what videos you watch. It puts up videos which it thinks you want to watch. No people do this. Software does this. YouTube wants to change this software. It wants to put up fewer videos of one type. People call them conspiracy theory videos. YouTube says that these videos show false information. What are these videos about? They can be about fake medicine . They can be about Flat Earth. They can be about events like 9/11 (the attacks on the World Trade Centre on September 11th 2011). Some people do not like this. They think that this is censorship . Difficult words: conspiracy theory (an explanation of things which is different from the explanation that most people believe; or saying something which is not true), fake medicine (medicine which does not help you), censorship (censoring – stopping what people can watch, write, read, or say). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fifteen-year-old Mason Ketly has a rare brain tumour that doctors found three months ago, and now he is going to receive pioneering cancer treatment at the UK’s first proton beam treatment centre. The proton beam can remove only the tumour and avoid damaging other parts of the brain. The new centre will help 750 people every year, and people plan to open a second one in London next year. Mason said that the machines were ‘beautiful-looking’ and ‘futuristic’, and he thinks that they will help him ‘really well’. He wants to be a doctor when he grows up. In 2014, the treatment centre was in the news when Ashya King’s parents took him out of a different hospital to take him out of the country to find a hospital that also had proton beam therapy. Difficult words: tumour (a mass of cells in your body that can become cancer), pioneering (innovative, very new), proton beam (a stream of tiny things called protons that have energy inside them). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Three months ago, a teenager’s doctors found a rare brain tumour in his brain. He is going to receive new cancer treatment at the UK’s first proton beam treatment centre. The proton beam targets the tumour exactly and does not damage other parts of the brain. The new centre will help 750 people a year, and people will open a second one in London next year. The teenager liked the proton beam machines and said that they were beautiful and looked like things from the future. He thinks that they will help him ‘really well’. He wants to be a doctor when he grows up. Difficult words: tumour (an extra part in your body which can become cancer), proton beam (a stream of tiny things like electricity that have energy inside them), target (aim at exactly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A teenager goes to hospital. Doctors find a brain tumour in his brain. They send him to get cancer treatment . He gets the treatment at a new centre. It is the first centre of this type in Britain. It uses new technology. The technology is very good. It destroys only the tumour. The rest of the brain is fine. The new centre can help 750 people a year. People are building another centre in London. It opens next year. The teenager likes the machines at the centre. He says that they are beautiful. He says that they look like things from the future. He wants to be a doctor when he grows up. Difficult words: brain tumour (an extra part in your body which can become cancer), cancer (when your body keeps growing tumours that can kill you; a very serious illness), treatment (making an ill person better). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Malaga, Spain, a two-year-old named Julen Rosello fell down a 110-metre borehole . Rescue efforts have been continuing for five days, and the work has been difficult due to the terrain . The rescue workers are on the side of a mountain, and there are hard rock formations that are slowing them down. Malaga’s local officials said that the rescue work will continue until people find Julen. Difficult words: borehole (a deep, narrow hole that people dig to find water or oil), terrain (the shape and the type of the ground), formation (how something has been shaped or formed over time). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Spain, a two-year-old fell down a 110-metre borehole . People started looking for the boy five days ago. The work is difficult because of the terrain . The rescue workers are on the side of a mountain, and there are hard rocks in the ground. They say that the rescue work will not stop until they find the boy. Difficult words: borehole (a deep, skinny hole that people make to find water or oil), terrain (how the ground looks and other physical features), rescue worker (a person who works to rescue – save somebody). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Spain, a babyboy falls down a borehole . People try to save him. They work for over five days. The work is very difficult. The terrain makes it hard. There are very hard rocks in the ground. People say that they will keep looking for the baby. They will stop when they find him. Difficult words: borehole (a deep, small hole that people make to find water or oil), terrain (what is in the ground and how it is looks), will (‘in the future’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Brumadinho Dam in Brazil burst at an iron ore mill, and a torrent of water submerged the area, killing people and destroying houses. At least 40 people died and hundreds are still missing as the search for survivors continues. However, the hopes of finding survivors are getting low. Some local residents returned to their homes to find them completely destroyed. Family and friends nervously wait for news of their missing loved ones. Vale, a huge company who owns and operates the dam, has been issued with an initial £50 million fine and £1.2 billion of its assets were frozen. This is the second dam to collapse in Brazil in recent years. The previous one collapsed in 2015 and killed 19 people. Difficult words: iron ore mill (where people make steel – a type of metal that we use to build things), submerge (put under water), huge (very big). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A disaster happened in Brazil when a dam burst , and covered an area with dirty water. People died and the water destroyed homes. At least 40 people are confirmed dead and hundreds are still missing. People are looking for survivors, but they do not have much hope. Some people returned to their homes, only to find them completely destroyed. Family and friends anxiously wait for news of their missing loved ones. Vale, a big company who owns and operates the dam was fined £50 million. Another £1.2 billion of its money was frozen. This is the second dam to collapse in Brazil in recent years. The previous one collapsed in 2015 and killed 19 people. Difficult words: dam (a wall which holds water and forms a lake), burst (break open), anxiously (nervously, they cannot wait). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is some bad news from Brazil. A dam bursts there. An area goes under dirty water. The water kills people. It destroys their homes. More than 40 people die. Hundreds of people are missing . There is not much hope for the missing people. This is not the first time that a dam bursts. This happens in 2015, too. That time, nineteen people die. Difficult words: dam (a wall which holds water and forms a lake), burst (break open), be missing (when you are missing, people do not know if you are alive and OK). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Gigantic sinkholes appeared in Iran, some as deep as 60 metres. They are the result of land sinkage caused by excessive water pumping. Iran relies heavily on agriculture to feed its 80-million percent population, meaning that there is great demand for water. Using up the groundwater can also lead to desertification, which is when the ground becomes more like a desert. Difficult words: gigantic (huge, very big), sinkage (sinking – falling down), excessive (extreme). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Large sinkholes appeared in Iran, and some are as deep as 60 metres. The ground sinks because people are pumping too much groundwater to use it to farm or to produce food for 80 million Iranians. However, as they pump the water, the ground is moving. Difficult words: appear (become, start to exist), pump (make the water go up), groundwater (water which is underground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sinkholes appear in Iran. Some are as deep as 60 metres. The ground sinks because people are moving too much groundwater up. People need the water to farm. They need to produce food for 80 million Iranians. However, as the water moves, the ground moves, too. Difficult words: sinkhole (a type of hole that happens when there is nothing to hold the ground up), appear (become, start to exist), sink (fall down), groundwater (water which is underground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sandstorms are common in Egypt during late winter and early spring, and an extreme one forced the closing of highways and the port of Alexandria. An orange cloud of sand plunged Cairo into darkness with winds reaching speeds of more than 50 kilometres per hour. Difficult words: common (normal), force (use power to make something happen), plunge (put underneath something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Sandstorms are common in Egypt during late winter and early spring. An extreme sandstorm hit the country recently, closing highways and the port of Alexandria. An orange cloud of sand plunged Cairo into darkness. The winds blow more than 50 kilometres per hour. Difficult words: common (normal), extreme (unusual), plunge (put under something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sandstorms are normal in Egypt in late winter and early spring. An extreme sandstorm hits the country. It closes highways. It closes the port of Alexandria, too. Cairo is in an orange cloud of sand. The winds blow more than 50 kilometres per hour. Difficult words: port (a city where boats can come), cloud (a mass), blow (move). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Donald Trump and Kim Kim Jong-un signed a vague denuclearisation agreement in June, but there has been no evidence of North Korea disassembling its missile program. Furthermore, Beyond Parallel looked into North Korea. Beyond Parallel is a self-described ‘ non-partisan or authoritative analytic’ project that the Centre for Strategic and International Studies sponsors. The project found a secret operational ballistic missile base in North Korea. The report says that this one is one of the oldest bases, and one of about 20 undeclared missile operating bases in the country. The World Economic Forum brings together some 2,500 top business leaders, international political leaders, economists, celebrities and journalists for up to four days to discuss the most pressing issues facing the world. It happens in Switzerland annually. Sir David Attenborough, an English broadcaster and natural historian, urged those in power to act on climate change before it is too late. He said that a lot of people realised the enormity of the problem only just now, but if we do not sort ourselves out within the next ten years, we are dooming our children and our grandchildren to a terrible future. He said that we have to think about difficult and painful things because if we do not, there is only going to be a bigger difficulty and bigger pain. Difficult words: issue (a problem), urge (ask, try to make somebody do something), enormity (the extreme seriousness of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
